tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תפילה לראש חודש טבת ותקופת החורף על חנוכּה
Prayer for the new moon of Ṭevet on Ḥanukkah occurring on the winter solstice, by Rabbi David Seidenberg (neohasid·org)

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer for the new moon of Ṭevet on Ḥanukkah occurring on the winter solstice, by Rabbi David Seidenberg (neohasid·org)

tei:lg.tei:l: Return again, return again
Return to the land of your soul (2×)
Return to who you are
Return to what you are
Return to where you are
born and reborn again
Return again, return again
Return to the land of your soul
In the depths of darkness,
the darkness of the new moon of Ḥanukkah,
and the darkness of the sun at solstice,
we call to You.
In the presence of these seeds of light of the sixth night,
we turn to You. As You turn the wheel of the sun,
as You draw back the darkness of the moon,
may You open gates for us, Potei’aḥ She’arim,
so that we may be drawn through these gates
into the holy mystery of darkness
and the glowing light of wisdom.
“Deep is calling unto deep, tehom el tehom qorei” (Psalms 42:8) —
may we be listening.
“The One who set darkness to be Her secret place, yashet ḥoshekh sit’ro” (Psalms 18:12) —
may You teach us to see the darkness
dancing between the flames of the candles,
and the darkness dancing within the flame,
so that we may cherish the Earth,
dancing between the sun and the moon,
the womb of all Life,
and see the radiance in all creatures,
in the passing of life into life,
deep into deep,
fall into winter into spring.
Barukh atah Adonai, blessed be You
the One who brings in the twilight and composes the evenings.
Barukh atah Adonai blessed be You,
the One who forms light and creates darkness,
former of all the heavens lights.
